record.provider: GBIF IPT via a data-hosting centre - free email account, but the payload must be biodiversity occurrences

free_tier.stated: No quota published anywhere: a data-hosting centre gives you an account on its IPT installation, and your dataset lives in that IPT's data directory. Capacity is whatever the centre provisioned; there is no per-user byte figure to quote.

egress.terms: Free public download as DwC-A; GBIF also mirrors a full monthly snapshot to AWS Open Data, Azure Planetary Computer and a public S3 bucket.

record.tooling: IPT web UI plus its REST resource endpoints; publishing to GBIF mints a DOI. VertNet (vertebrates), VLIZ/EurOBIS (marine, 20+ IPT instances), BioFresh (freshwater) are the listed centres.
record.chaining: Per dataset within a centre's IPT; multiple datasets are allowed, but reviewers police relevance, so this does not shard.
record.limits_note: Scope restricted to occurrence, checklist, and sampling-event data in Darwin Core format. Registration is coordinated by contacting the data centre or GBIF helpdesk. No explicit byte cap is stated in published documentation.
record.reliability_note: Long-lived EU-funded centres with backed-up IPT data directories; the IPT is a metadata+archive publisher, not an object store, and it re-packages rather than serving your original bytes.

evidence.proved: 'A data-hosting centre (DHC) can provide users with an account on their IPT installation'; requirements list includes 'Ensuring the IPT data directory is regularly backed up'
